title: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
prompt:
Return the maximum depth of a binary tree — the number of nodes on the longest root-to-leaf path.

**Example**: `[3,9,20,null,null,15,7]` → `3`.
hints: If you already knew the depth of the left subtree and of the right subtree, how would you get the depth of the whole tree?
An empty tree (`root == null`) has depth 0. That's the base case.

solution.explanation: This is the clearest case of trusting the recursion: assume `maxDepth` is correct on the subtrees, and the tree's depth is one more than the deeper of the two. Every node is visited once, O(n) time; the stack grows to O(h), which is O(n) for a skewed tree.
